No, the claim in that X post is **not true**—I misunderstood the content earlier.

The post from Rep. Kelly Morrison (D-MN) criticizes House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA) for **not bringing a vote** on legislation to extend enhanced Affordable Care Act (ACA/Obamacare) premium tax credits, which are set to expire at the end of 2025. Without an extension, millions of Americans who buy insurance through the ACA marketplaces could face sharply higher premiums starting in 2026 (estimates suggest average increases of hundreds of dollars per month for many).

### What actually happened:
- In mid-December 2025, House Republicans, led by Speaker Johnson, advanced and passed their own healthcare bill (the "Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act" or similar GOP package). It focused on measures like promoting employer-sponsored plans, association health plans, pharmacy benefit manager transparency, and other cost-control tweaks—claiming it would reduce premiums by around 11% overall.
- **It did not include an extension** of the enhanced ACA subsidies (originally boosted during the pandemic and extended through 2025).
- Johnson explicitly refused to allow a separate vote on a bipartisan or Democratic proposal to extend those subsidies (for 3 years or temporarily).
- This led to internal GOP tension: A few moderate Republicans joined Democrats in a discharge petition to force a vote on subsidy extension, but it didn't come to the floor before the year ended.
- The House passed the GOP bill narrowly (mostly party-line), but it's unclear if the Senate took it up or if it addressed the immediate subsidy cliff.

Morrison's post accurately reflects that Johnson blocked a direct vote on extending the ACA credits, prioritizing the Republican alternative instead. Her pairing it with criticism of RFK Jr. (as HHS Secretary) canceling certain children's health research grants is separate political commentary.

In short: Johnson **did refuse** to bring up the ACA subsidy extension for a vote, aligning with the post's claim on that point. My previous response was based on a complete misreading of the post's actual text.
